title: How many more boxes of sleep on a holiday?
description: Eight hours of sleep on a weekday and ten hours on a holiday are turned into boxes on two strips. The video compares the strips and breaks Keeko's doubt that four more boxes means four more hours.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare two strips by their boxes, and turn the extra boxes back into hours by halving. Watch for students who read the extra boxes as extra hours.

source: You sleep 8 hours on a weekday and 10 hours on a holiday. Ho
video_script.why: The child has turned hours into boxes and now compares two strips and turns the extra boxes back into hours.
video_script.substitution: Multiply each sleep time by two for its boxes, take the smaller from the larger, and halve to get hours.
video_script.anchor: two strips of forty eight boxes, one for a weekday and one for a holiday, with the sleep boxes coloured
video_script.wrong_answer: four more boxes is four more hours
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko finds four more boxes and calls them four more hours, forgetting that a box is half an hour.
video_script.payoff_line: the holiday strip has four more boxes and that is two more hours

final_answer.value: 16 boxes and 20 boxes; 4 more boxes, which is 2 more hours, on the holiday
final_answer.spoken: the weekday has sixteen boxes of sleep and the holiday has twenty boxes; the holiday strip has four more boxes and that is two more hours

maths_rules: weekday: 8 x 2 = 16 boxes; holiday: 10 x 2 = 20 boxes
20 - 16 = 4 more boxes on the holiday; 4 boxes x half an hour = 2 hours, matching 10 - 8 = 2 hours
slip: a box is half an hour, so the extra boxes are not extra hours
video_script.design: One idea: boxes for each sleep time, take away, then halve to get hours. The wrong idea is that an extra box is an extra hour. Two strips stay on screen all video, with the sleep boxes coloured.
